description_full: Northrim BanCorp, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for Northrim Bank that provides commercial banking products and services to businesses and professional individuals. It operates through three segments: Community Banking, Home Mortgage Lending, and Specialty Finance. The company offers noninterest-bearing checking accounts and interest-bearing time deposits, checking and savings accounts, individual retirement and money market deposit accounts, certificates of deposit, and business sweep accounts. It also provides short and medium-term commercial loans, commercial credit lines, construction and real estate loans, and consumer loans, as well as short and medium-term working capital. In addition, the company offers consumer and business online banking, mobile app, and mobile deposits; and debit and credit cards. Further, it provides mobile web and app banking, consumer online account opening, personal finance, online documents, consumer debit cards, business debit cards, my rewards for consumer debit cards, retail lockbox services, card control, corporate purchase cards, integrated payables, home equity advantage access cards, telebanking, and automated teller services. Additionally, the company offers personalized checks at account opening, overdraft protection from a savings account, commercial drive-up banking, automatic transfer and payment, external transfer, bill pay, wire transfer, direct payroll deposit, electronic tax payment, automated clearing house origination and receipt, remote deposit capture, account reconciliation and positive pay, merchant, cash management, annuity, and long-term investment portfolio products and services. It also provides investment advisory, trust, wealth management, factoring, and mortgage services. The company was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in Anchorage, Alaska.

financial_summary: Northrim BanCorp Inc is a small-cap financial services business with a $533M market cap on $256M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +26% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 9% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 80% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $134M in free cash flow — roughly 52 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.1× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield of 2.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 3.0% of the shares.

sect: Its 33% operating margin is roughly in line with the Financial Services median (29%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.27x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+2.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 514 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 6% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 10% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 22% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 32% and a beta of 0.79, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.20 vs 5y 0.71), so read it loosely.
About $3.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 51% in the 2020 crash, 16% in the 2022 bear market and 69% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 40% below its DCF fair value of $39.77, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 19%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $32.31 to $50.22 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Financial Services peers: P/E 9.7 vs 12.3 and P/FCF 4.0 vs 13.0 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 4% above its 10-year median.
The 3 covering analysts target $28.33 on average, 18% above the price.
The price implies 16.7% annual cash-flow growth, 9pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 14% earns above the cost of capital of 8.7%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.52).
It runs a 80% gross margin and converts 52% of revenue into free cash flow.
It earns a 20% return on equity.
Operating margin is running 5pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The Beneish M-score (-2.18) sits just under the manipulation line, so earnings quality bears watching.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 25.5% over 3 years, 13.8% over 5 years and 9.7% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 18%).
At current returns, reinvesting 3% of profits supports about 0.4% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Analysts expect 7.1% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.0%, and institutions hold 77%.
Insider trading is two-way: 5 purchases and 8 sales over the past year, net $469K sold.
It returns 2.6% a year to shareholders (2.7% in dividends, less 0.1% of net share issuance).
The share count has shrunk 1.6% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 30 consecutive years, raising it 10.5% a year over the last five.
people: With about 516 employees, each generates about $495K of revenue, in line with the Financial Services median, and revenue has grown 11.5% a year across its filed history.
